added_claim_errors: Quotes the employer's right as limited to 「業務の正常な運営を妨げる場合」; the statute (and the Shizuoka Labour Bureau page A itself links, which I opened) says 「事業の正常な運営」. Minor misquote.

Tells her to check the day is treated as 「事前に承認された休暇」 rather than 欠勤. There is no such legal category: leave that is not paid leave (or a special leave set by the work rules) is still an unpaid absence, so the advice misleads.
「直前だと時季変更権の余地が広がります」: a plausible reading of case law, stated without support (judged from my own knowledge, not checked).

reasons: Both answers start by correcting the manager and give the right figures: paid leave is granted on October 1 after six months, it is 5 days, and she must have attended at least 80% of her workdays. Neither explicitly calls it the reduced (proportional) grant for part-timers. A's LINE message asks to take a specific date as paid leave, politely and without confrontation. A also gives a reply to use if the manager refuses again and says the shop can only move the date, not refuse it. B's correction ends at the explanation: it tells her not to raise paid leave in the LINE at all. Its main and short messages are plain requests for a day off that offer to make up the shift, which leaves the manager's wrong premise in place, and it adds an invented category, 「事前に承認された休暇」. Point 7 is the deliverable the key centres on, and A gets it right while B gets it wrong, so A wins decisively.
